The blue-on-blue circular firing squad at rapey Cornell University marches on with the news that one of the seven frat brothers accused of participating in the alleged gang rape of Jane Doe told the campus police that he was her victim that night.

According to far-left ABC News, former Cornell student and Chi Phi frat brother Matthew Ingalls told the Cornell police that “he was too intoxicated to consent and suggested that Jane Doe actually assaulted him.” Ingalls is now one of the seven former Cornell students named in Jane Doe’s civil suit filed a few weeks ago alleging a gang rape.

Ingalls, however, made his claim two years ago, in November of 2024, when campus cops investigated the alleged event about three weeks after it occurred.

This case is such a mess, so I’ll try to make it make some sense…

In the early morning hours of October 20, 2024, either a gang rape took place, or a disgusting night of voluntary degeneracy involving hours of group sex (one 20-year-old woman known only as Jane Doe and a number of guys), illegal drugs, and underage drinking.

About three weeks later, Jane Doe went to the campus police to report the incident, BUT, according to the local district attorney (a Democrat named Matthew Van Houten), her statement made clear that she was a willing participant in the alcohol, drugs, and sex. Nothing happened without her consent. Therefore, no charges were pursued.

In the weeks between the night in question and the report to campus police, Jane Doe exchanged text messages with members of the frat that appear to back up the claim that everything that happened was consensual. In fact, in one text message, she outright wrote: “none of the sexual stuff was illegal.” She also expressed interest in getting together again with one of the guys and was eager to return to the frat house for a Halloween party.

Then she was disinvited from the frat party and angry that news of the night had spread around campus. Two years later, just weeks before the national midterm elections, and with a ton of corporate media fanfare, Jane Doe filed a massive civil suit against the seven men, against Cornell, and against her own sorority (for allowing her to drink while underage).

What I find most fascinating about this is that, based on what we know now, the only person who reported an assault at the time was… one of the guys… Matthew Ingalls… who claimed Jane Doe took advantage of him when he could not consent.

“Within two days of reporting the incident to police,” reports ABC, “Jane Doe contacted Ingalls and two other men allegedly involved in the incident to get their assessment of what happened that evening.”

“If I just know what happened, then I can feel a little bit better and move on and maybe be able to stay at this school,” she said in the recorded call.
